target.name: American Housing Corporation
target.founder: Bobby Fijan, Riley Meik, Harris Rothaermel, William Davis

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $200K total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
American Housing Corporation is a pre-seed stage company in the housing and construction sector, founded by Bobby Fijan, Riley Meik, Harris Rothaermel, and William Davis. The company has raised $200K to date. No comparable public or private companies were identified in the available dataset, limiting the ability to apply market-based valuation approaches.

Given the absence of comparable company data, stage-progression methodology provides the primary valuation anchor. Using total capital raised ($200K) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of pre-seed to seed-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $500K. This represents the most defensible point estimate given data constraints.

The triangulated range of $425K (low) to $575K (high) reflects reasonable variance around this central estimate, with the $500K median supported by stage-appropriate progression mechanics. Material uncertainties remain substantial: the absence of comparable transactions in housing and construction limits calibration of the step-up multiplier, and no traction metrics (revenue, user adoption, or product milestones) are available to stress-test the valuation. Any investment decision should be heavily weighted toward qualitative assessment of team, product-market fit, and capital efficiency metrics not captured in this analysis.
